root_cause.text: The PN533 UART receive path (`pn532_receive_buf()` in `drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c`) kept appending bytes to `dev->recv_skb` for incomplete/malformed traffic without enforcing a hard length check, so a stream with no valid PN532 frame header could grow the skb until the tail limit was reached.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `pn532_receive_buf()` “appends every incoming byte to dev->recv_skb” and only resets it after `pn532_uart_rx_is_frame()` sees a complete frame, allowing “malformed UART traffic” to grow past `PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN`; the patch fixes this by adding `if (unlikely(!skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb))) skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0);` before `skb_put_u8()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The PN533 UART receive path (`pn532_receive_buf()` in `drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c`) kept appending bytes to `dev->recv_skb` for incomplete/malformed traffic without enforcing a hard length check, so a stream with no valid PN532 frame header could grow the skb until the tail limit was reached.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says `pn532_receive_buf()` “appends every incoming byte to dev->recv_skb” and only resets it after `pn532_uart_rx_is_frame()` sees a complete frame, allowing “malformed UART traffic” to grow past `PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN`; the patch fixes this by adding `if (unlikely(!skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb))) skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0);` before `skb_put_u8()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a safeguard in PN532 UART receive handling to avoid skb overflow by resetting a full receive buffer before appending more data.
intent_record.what: Inside pn532_receive_buf(), a new check was added at the start of the per-byte receive loop: if dev->recv_skb has no tailroom, skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0) is called before appending the next byte with skb_put_u8().
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the driver from writing past the end of the receive skb when additional serial data arrives after the buffer is full. Instead of overflowing, the skb is reset to an empty state and byte accumulation continues safely.

grouping_result.intent: Add a safeguard in PN532 UART receive handling to avoid skb overflow by resetting a full receive buffer before appending more data.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a safeguard in the PN532 UART receive path to prevent unbounded skb growth when receiving malformed or incomplete data, addressing the lack of a hard length check.

candidates.rationale: This appends every received byte to dev->recv_skb unconditionally, with no hard length check or buffer reset before growth, which matches the root cause of the skb growing until the tail limit on malformed/incomplete traffic.
This loop processes each incoming byte in sequence, and in the vulnerable path it allows repeated appends to the receive skb without bounding growth when no valid frame header is found.
The frame-validation check occurs after the byte has already been appended, so malformed traffic can still enlarge the skb repeatedly before any rejection or reset happens.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement appends each received byte to dev->recv_skb unconditionally. In the vulnerable receive path, malformed or incomplete traffic could keep growing the skb without a hard length check or reset, leading to tail-limit exhaustion.

This loop drives byte-by-byte accumulation of incoming data. Combined with the unconditional append inside the loop, it enables repeated growth of the receive skb for streams that never form a valid PN532 frame header.

The frame check happens only after bytes have already been appended. That ordering allows malformed traffic to enlarge dev->recv_skb before any rejection or buffer reset occurs, matching the root cause.

Author: Lars Poeschel <poeschel@lemonage.de>

    nfc: pn533: add UART phy driver
    
    This adds the UART phy interface for the pn533 driver.
    The pn533 driver can be used through UART interface this way.
    It is implemented as a serdev device.
    
    Cc: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable receive path logic is present in this new UART driver. In `pn532_receive_buf()` the code unconditionally appends every incoming byte with `skb_put_u8(dev->recv_skb, *data++);` and only then checks `if (!pn532_uart_rx_is_frame(dev->recv_skb)) continue;`. There is no hard length bound or reset for malformed/no-header traffic before appending, so a stream without a valid PN532 frame header can keep growing `dev->recv_skb` until the skb tail limit is reached. The buffer is only initialized with `alloc_skb(PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN, GFP_KERNEL);`, but there is no logic here enforcing that limit during reception. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present in this commit.
